key_claims: Introduces a continuous 3-D latent diffusion model framework for CT and MRI generation and reconstruction.
Uses a compact autoencoder with a coordinate-conditioned local implicit image function decoder.
On high-resolution CT, the proposed autoencoder is approximately 12-32 times faster than reference autoencoders and uses the lowest peak GPU memory.
The frozen 3-D latent prior generates coherent full volumes without visible patch seams.
Can be applied to sparse-view CT and accelerated MRI reconstruction without task-specific retraining.
Direct pixel-domain reconstruction remains more accurate than the latent prior approach.
limitations: The proposed autoencoder shows a moderate reduction in voxel-level accuracy compared to reference autoencoders.
Direct pixel-domain reconstruction is more accurate than the latent prior approach.
The framework is evaluated on specific volume sizes (CT 512^3, MRI 256^3) and may not generalize to other resolutions.
The source is an arXiv preprint and may not have undergone full peer review.
what_not_to_say: The framework is clinically validated or approved for medical use.
The latent prior approach is more accurate than direct pixel-domain reconstruction.
The framework is faster than all existing methods in all scenarios.
The framework can be used for other imaging modalities beyond CT and MRI.
The code is currently available at the provided GitHub link.
